tool_call_format: atem: a <atem:function_calls><atem:invoke name="f"><atem:parameter name="k">v</atem:parameter></atem:invoke></atem:function_calls> block, regex-parsed, inside a `<|start|>assistant to=<tool><|message|>` turn; tool results are `<|start|>tool <name><|message|><tool_output name="<name>">...</tool_output><|eot|>`
known_template_errors: Onyx ATEM chat template requires tool_call.function.arguments to be a dict (mapping); a JSON string cannot be parsed in the HF jinja sandbox.
notes: Template reads reasoning_strength, not reasoning_effort, and validates nothing: any string renders as the literal line 'Reasoning strength: <value>.' The template has no enable_thinking or thinking handling, so thinking_on and thinking_off render byte-identical prompts (verified). b11960's caps_apply_reasoning_effort binds reasoning_effort and reasoning_strength to the same value (common/jinja/caps.cpp:31-36), so OpenAI reasoning_effort does reach the prompt. reasoning_effort "none" is dropped by the server (server-common.cpp:1497-1506), so it falls back to the template default "high": sending none means high reasoning, not none. A developer role renders without error but the message is silently dropped (output equals a plain user turn). Tool calls must carry object arguments; a JSON string raises.
